findings.finding: The Alia earn-out is tracking toward its maximum: ARR rose 45% in four months (£6.9m to £10.0m), and the deal pays up to US$30m more in cash over two years if Alia 'maintains its historical growth rate'. Against £17.1m of year-end cash, the FY26 balance sheet will carry a large contingent liability for the first time (Alia completed after the interim period).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior earn-out disclosure on a results day. The Social Snowball deal and trading update of 26 Jun 2025 moved +4.4%, and the Alia acquisition RNS (4 Mar 2026) sat inside the interim window (10 Mar, -4.3%).
findings.original_quote: up to $30m in contingent cash consideration over two years, payable if Alia maintains its historical growth rate at sufficiently accretive margins for the Group
findings.why_not_priced: The terms and the ARR are both public, so the arithmetic is available to anyone. What is not yet public is the booked fair value and the cash bridge, i.e. how much FY27 cash is committed and whether that limits the dividend or buybacks. If the market had priced a near-maximum payout as a capital squeeze, I would expect a dividend-cut debate in previews, and I found none. Financing question answered: the money buys ARR growing about 45% at no more than 2x forward ARR, which is why the sign is only mildly negative.
